claims.text: The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers symptoms of treating a Pulumi Output as if it were already a plain value.

In Pulumi, using an Output<T> as if it were a plain value (e.g., string conversion) produces placeholder text such as 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi produces the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when concurrent updates occur.
x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon can cause crashes or hangs with Pulumi.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
The Pulumi CLI emits `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

In Pulumi, converting an output value to a string directly (instead of via apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; it silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In Pulumi TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output in an f-string produces text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
Pulumi Python provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In Pulumi C#, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes Pulumi (TypeScript, Python, and C#) throw an exception when an output is converted to a string, instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi output evaluates the output object and is generally always true regardless of the resolved value.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an Output<bool> is not a bool.
Values known at program start, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the output object itself.
A `StackReference` lets one Pulumi stack consume another stack's outputs.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value out of an output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).
